questions.question_text: What is a key step to avoid plagiarism when paraphrasing or summarizing, as discussed in the chapter?

options.text: Changing just a few words without understanding the original idea
Rewriting the content in your own words and citing the source
Copying the original text and adding quotation marks
Using the idea without mentioning where it came from

correct_answer.text: Rewriting the content in your own words and citing the source

questions.question_text: When should you use a direct quote in your writing, according to the chapter?

options.text: For every piece of information you find from a source
Only when the original wording is impactful or precise and worth highlighting
Whenever you want to make your essay longer
When you don’t have time to paraphrase or summarize

correct_answer.text: Only when the original wording is impactful or precise and worth highlighting

questions.question_text: What is an effective way to integrate sources into your writing, as explained in the chapter?

options.text: Copying large sections of text without any citation
Using signal phrases like “According to” and connecting the source to your own ideas
Listing all sources at the end without mentioning them in the text
Ignoring sources and focusing only on your opinions

correct_answer.text: Using signal phrases like “According to” and connecting the source to your own ideas

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common citation mistake to avoid, based on the chapter’s guidance?

options.text: Citing every borrowed idea or quote immediately after using it
Forgetting to include a citation after paraphrasing a source’s idea
Double-checking the format of your citation style for accuracy
Including full details of the source in your bibliography

correct_answer.text: Forgetting to include a citation after paraphrasing a source’s idea
